### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-datasource`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via DatasourceAdminServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/odata-datasources.mdx`  _(via DatasourceAdminServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6440384440b929c889a0aef080fb0f4537d3c4bc` — the merge of head `2e46f1637f33ef14359ec783959fea38419b2016` into base `6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6440384440b929c889a0aef080fb0f4537d3c4bc && git checkout 6440384440b929c889a0aef080fb0f4537d3c4bc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77 2e46f1637f33ef14359ec783959fea38419b2016 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77 && git merge --no-ff 2e46f1637f33ef14359ec783959fea38419b2016

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6f7df530cd1432d0d34e0ee5cbee6b4d669e3f77` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2e46f1637f33ef14359ec783959fea38419b2016`
Local-runs: none
Scope: narrowing face, no path `hits`; floor = every diff path outside the prose face: `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-update-kept-pool-stores-nothing.test.ts`, `packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/datasource-empty-secret-refusal.test.ts`, `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` + cited code read (not reviewed): `datasource-connection-service.ts` (`connect`, `recordState`, `availabilityOf`, `disconnect`, `reconnect`, `amendRetainedReason`), `admin-routes.ts` (`splitSecret`, the `/test`, POST and PATCH doors), `index.ts` (export list), `datasource-secret-binder.ts` (`write` mints `sys_secret:<handle.id>` per call), `package.json` `exports`, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` `rehydratePools`/`convergePool`, `__tests__/datasource-update-rebuild.test.ts` (a void-answering seam); the prose face `.changeset/29879-datasource-update-kept-pool-stores-nothing.md` read for ②; precedent #28928 = PR #29064 (merge `0a41075a`, changeset `28928-empty-datasource-secret-refused.md`, its `assertSecretNotEmpty` hunk) read via the API because the local clone is shallow; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` (`reviewFace`), `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`CATEGORIES`, `no-migration-prescription`) for the grammar.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset), no published schema. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **No-persist on a kept pool: correct, one write path.** At head `updateDatasource` seals the new secret (`newRef`), rebuilds through `tryReregisterPool(existing, merged)`, and on `previousPoolKept` calls `discardUnstoredSecret` and returns `toSummary(existing)` before `putDatasourceRecord` and before `publishDatasourceMutation`. So no key of the patch (record, `external.credentialsRef`, `label`, `config`, …) reaches the store, the row sealed for the patch is removed when `newRef !== prevRef`, and no cluster signal is published (the plugin resets `livePoolRecords` to `previous`). The answer is the retained `failed`/`blocked` verdict with `reconnect`'s "NOT in force" suffix, which is now true. Judged right.
- **Success path unchanged in effect.** The old guard `if (prevRef && prevRef !== credentialsRef) tryRemoveSecret(prevRef)` becomes `if (newRef && prevRef && prevRef !== newRef) tryRemoveSecret(prevRef)` after the single `putDatasourceRecord`: same condition, later position. `active: false` (store → unregister) and the no-connectivity-change register (store → `registerPool`) keep their order. The new `putDatasourceRecord` catch removes the unreferenced `newRef` and rethrows; the stored record still names the working `prevRef`, which was not removed. Judged right.
- **Ordering hazards.** The old order (seal → remove old → put → rebuild) could lose the working credential on a crash between remove and put; the new order (seal → rebuild → put → remove old) cannot. A crash before the decision, or between seal and `discardUnstoredSecret`, leaves at most an orphan encrypted `sys_secret` row with no referrer, and the stored record keeps pointing at the working row. A failing `removeSecret` on the discard path is `warn` + orphan, the pre-existing `tryRemoveSecret` shape. Strictly safer than before; no must-fix.
- **POST takes its own path, unchanged.** `createDatasource` still seals → puts → `tryRegisterPool`; there is no previous pool and the create answer never says "NOT in force", so the kept-pool rule does not apply. Only `assertSecretNotEmpty` moves on that door. Judged right.
- **Misdetection of "kept".** The plugin's reading is `getConnectionState(name).availability !== 'available' && getDriverByName(name) !== undefined`, taken after `reconnect` settles. A successful rebuild records `connected` ⇒ `available` ⇒ not kept ⇒ stored (pinned by the control). A failed rebuild with no live pool to keep (inactive, or failed at boot) is a plain `connect` whose rollback evicts its own registration ⇒ no driver ⇒ not kept ⇒ stored with a plain `error`, as before. An engine without `getDriverByName` never produces a kept pool in `reconnect` either, so the two readings agree. A `skipped-policy` (`blocked`) rebuild is also "kept" and stores nothing, consistent with `reconnect` appending the same suffix. Judged sound for the default seam.
- **Second failing PATCH.** The first leaves `failed` + the old driver re-registered; the second evicts, fails, restores ⇒ kept ⇒ nothing stored. Pinned. Judged right.
- **Host seam that answers nothing / throws.** `outcome?.previousPoolKept === true` reads `void` as `false`; a throwing seam is warned and read as `false`; the pre-#13804 fallback (`registerPool` only) returns `false`. All three keep today's "store whatever the rebuild did"; the existing `datasource-update-rebuild.test.ts` and the #28928 harness's void seam still pass untouched. The return type `Promise<ReregisterPoolOutcome | void> | ReregisterPoolOutcome | void` keeps every `() => Promise<void>` implementer compiling. Judged right.
- **Rewrite-in-place binder.** When `newRef === prevRef` the discard path removes nothing and logs once at `error` with the remedy; the shipped binder mints `sys_secret:<handle.id>` per write, so the branch is unreachable with it. Degradation level is right for a durability loss.
- **Whitespace refusal.** Same module function `assertSecretNotEmpty`, same two call sites (create after the name check, update after the undeclared-key / inline-`ssl.key` checks, both before any write, as in #28928), same message text and the same `400 DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR` via `badRequest`. `splitSecret` normalises `"\t\n"` and `{ value: "\t\n" }` alike. `typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim() !== ''` returns for every value the old `value !== ''` returned for, plus refuses blank strings; ` x\t` is sealed as sent (pinned on `written`). Judged right.
- **Widening.** `DatasourceAdminServiceConfig` is exported from `index.ts`; `reregisterPool`'s answer may now carry `{ previousPoolKept }`. `ReregisterPoolOutcome` is not named in the index but is reachable from the entry type graph through that member, so it is part of the published accept set; the PR declares the widening on the right symbol. Judged right.

### ② Semver level
`patch` on `@objectstack/service-datasource` with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both PR body and changeset, line-initial. `yes (narrowing)` is the documented spelling for a diff that widens one surface (`reregisterPool`'s answer) and narrows another (blank `secret` refused): `clause2-line.mjs`; `reviewFace` maps any `(narrowing)` arm to this face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. `secret` is split off the body before the draft is judged and never appears in `/api/v1/meta/datasource`, so `none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change keeps its BANNER and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md step 3). Title carries `!`. Changeset: `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing …`, Before / Now / Who moves, **The remedy** (leave `secret` out or `null`; send the new credential), marker `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->`, the same shape #28928 shipped and passed `check-adr-0087-registration` with. `Skills-docs: none — …` present in the PR body. Declaration consistent with the diff and the changeset level. The seat Claim's `Clause-②: no` is superseded by the committed tree; the PR body explains the departure. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no non-fleet login to name.
- Dev `open_questions`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: (1) a host binder resealing under the same ref cannot have the working credential restored; answered in ① (unreachable with the shipped binder; logged at `error`), no card owed. (2) the attribution block names the card thread; not a contract matter.
- Concurrent PATCHes on one name are not serialised; a bad PATCH finishing after a good one could read `available` and store. Pre-existing on this door (the old code stored unconditionally), not a regression of this diff; not a must-fix.
- `ReregisterPoolOutcome` is reachable but not re-exported from `index.ts`; optional follow-up, not blocking.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains three rows for the new rig's engine doubles: a ledger pin, no contract face.

### ④ Narrowing face
- The narrowing (blank `secret` refused at POST and PATCH) takes no declared capability away: the card measured that a whitespace-only rotation breaks the datasource at the next connect exactly as `""` did, and the change makes the "Nothing was written" refusal real for the one blank shape that slipped past #28928. Same guard, same message, same position relative to every write. Holds.
- The no-persist change against the card's reproduction (steps 2–7): the new rig drives the REAL plugins and REAL routes over one store, PATCHes a wrong password plus a `label`, asserts `200` / `error` / "NOT in force", `atRest(store)` (record and `sys_secret` ids) equal to before, `/test` ok on the kept pool, then a second boot over the same store whose `/test` is ok and whose factory built exactly `[REAL_PASSWORD]`. A failing `config` change and a second failing PATCH are pinned the same way; the control pins the working rotation stored, in force, old row retired, restart ok.
- Red on main / ablations as reported: 7 red on main (3 kept-pool, 4 blank); ablating `if (previousPoolKept)` reds exactly the 3 kept-pool pins, ablating `.trim()` reds exactly the 4 blank pins. Meaningful.
- Gaps, none blocking: no explicit pin that a void-answering seam still stores (covered indirectly), no pin for the `putDatasourceRecord`-throws branch removing `newRef`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-m2ruaq`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: PASS**
